ak-docs.tagline: Create, refresh, summarize, or audit evidence-based project docs.
ak-docs.summary: ak:docs reads the codebase and keeps the smallest doc set that explains purpose, contracts, and operations; docs own WHY/WHERE, code owns WHAT/HOW. Writing nothing is a valid result, and it never writes product code.
howItWorks: Opens with a short brainstorm: readers, outcome, evidence sources, acceptance criteria; reuses an accepted plan if present.
Routes on the first word (init, update, summarize, agent-context, agents, llms); empty input triggers a question.
Discovers docs from AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, README, docs/, then source, tests, and scripts; explicit routes override discovery.
init/update write via docs-manager; agents mines git and CI for DO/DON'T rules and asks for diff approval.
Verifies every path, command, and claim, then reports created, changed, kept, and deleted files.
useWhen: Onboard a repo with no docs (init) or reconcile docs after a merge changed contracts (update).
Write, audit, or tighten the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (agent-context, agents).
Generate or refresh llms.txt/llms-full.txt (llms), or get an evidence-backed summary (summarize).
avoidWhen: Subfolder context: use ak-folder-context.
Content comes from the user's own decisions, not code: use ak-interview-docs.
You want a chronological session log: use ak-journal.

params.name: init
params.desc: Set up a minimal project-specific doc route; no placeholders or template-only ADRs. Proposes the route before replacing existing docs.

params.name: update
params.desc: Reconcile affected docs with current evidence; edits only affected surfaces and removes stale or duplicate content.

params.name: summarize
params.desc: Summarize current evidence; writes a file only when the project defines one or the user asks.

params.name: agent-context
params.desc: Write, audit, or optimize the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md with a keep-or-cut filter.

params.name: agents
params.desc: Mine git and CI for recurring failures, distill DO/DON'T rules. Default 90 days/300 commits, 200 CI runs; implies --advice, needs diff approval.

params.name: [bound]
params.desc: agents only: override the window with days (agents 30d) or a commit count (agents 500).

params.name: llms
params.desc: Generate or update llms.txt and llms-full.txt per llmstxt.org, in the public/static folder if present, else repo root.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Spawn kongming for keep/cut/restructure advice before writing; the skill owns all edits. Implied by agents.

params.name: --audit
params.desc: agent-context/agents: kongming audits, then you decide keep/cut/fix one question at a time; only confirmed changes apply.

params.name: --dry-run
params.desc: agents only: stop after signal ranking and report; no advisor, no writes.

params.name: --source
params.desc: agents only: add a read-only source-tree pass via ak:scout alongside git/CI. Combines with --dry-run and --audit.

params.name: --preset classic
params.desc: init only: use the classic docs/ file names (project-overview-pdr.md, code-standards.md, and so on); files without real content are skipped.

examples.note: New repo without docs; the skill designs the smallest route.
Clean docs that drifted after a refactor.
Preview 30 days of recurring-failure signals without writing.

tips: Always name the operation; without one the skill asks instead of running init.
No new durable guidance means no-op: no timestamp bumps or cosmetic rewrites.
agents needs gh auth for CI signals; otherwise it uses git only.
artifacts: Doc files under docs/ plus a docs index when needed
Operational route records in the project's operational guide

ak-docs-seeker.tagline: Look up current library and framework docs via context7.com llms.txt.
ak-docs-seeker.summary: ak:docs-seeker classifies your query, fetches the library's llms.txt from context7.com, and suggests a parallel reading plan. Without llms.txt it falls back to cloning the repo and packing it with Repomix.
howItWorks: Runs detect-topic.js to classify the query, then fetch-docs.js to fetch llms.txt (topic, then general).
For many URLs, analyze-llms-txt.js ranks them and suggests 1, 3, or 7 parallel reader agents.
Last resort: clones the GitHub repo to /tmp and packs it with Repomix.
useWhen: You need the latest API and model knowledge may be stale.
Focused topic question (about 10-15 s) or broad framework coverage for planning (30-60 s).
avoidWhen: Generating llms.txt for your own project: use ak-llms or /ak:docs llms.
Comparing solutions or architectures: use ak-research.
Questions about internal code: use ak-scout.

params.name: [library-name]
params.desc: Library or framework to look up (next.js, shadcn); extracted from the query.

params.name: [topic]
params.desc: Specific topic: fast topic search (2-3 URLs). Omitted: general library search (8+ URLs).

examples.note: Topic query; returns 2-3 relevant URLs.
Library overview with a suggested parallel reading plan.

tips: Pass the official docs URL if you know it to skip discovery.
Repo analysis takes 5-10 min and many tokens; use it only without llms.txt.
Optional .env keys: CONTEXT7_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN (higher rate limits), GEMINI_API_KEY.
agents: Parallel reader agents as suggested by analyze-llms-txt.js (source names no specific subagent type)
artifacts: No fixed files; repo fallback clones into /tmp/docs-analysis and writes repomix-output.xml

ak-document-skills.tagline: Read, create, and edit Office files: docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx.
ak-document-skills.summary: ak:document-skills routes by format to the Word, PDF, PowerPoint, or spreadsheet workflow and returns a validated file. It preserves templates and existing content.
howItWorks: Detects the format and loads ak-docx, ak-pdf, ak-pptx, or ak-xlsx.
docx/pptx: create, edit via OOXML, or extract; keeps styles, comments, tracked changes, masters, and notes.
pdf: extract, create, merge/split/rotate, fill forms, OCR; checks pages and fillable fields.
xlsx: pandas for data, openpyxl for formulas; recalc.py recalculates and fixes formula errors.
Validates and renders each file; missing renderers are reported, not faked.
useWhen: Create a Word report or edit a contract with tracked changes.
Extract PDF tables, merge/split PDFs, or fill PDF forms.
Build a .pptx deck on a template or an .xlsx with formulas and charts.
avoidWhen: Reading long markdown in a browser: use ak-markdown-novel-viewer.
HTML presentation pages: use ak-show-off or ak-preview.
Image OCR/vision the model can't handle: consider ak-ai-multimodal.

params.name: <docx|pdf|pptx|xlsx>
params.desc: Required: format to process; selects the child skill.

params.name: [path]
params.desc: Input or output file path.

params.name: [action]
params.desc: docx/pptx: create|edit|extract; pdf: extract|create|merge|split|fill; xlsx: create|edit|analyze.

examples.note: Edit a contract with tracked changes.
Analyze sales data and add summary formulas.

tips: openpyxl writes formulas without values; run recalc.py (needs LibreOffice) or cells open empty.
Empty extraction from a scanned PDF needs OCR, not a 'no content' conclusion.
artifacts: Layout-check renders (when a renderer is available)

ak-folder-context.tagline: Create a compact subfolder CLAUDE.md plus linked AGENTS.md.
ak-folder-context.summary: ak:folder-context writes durable context for one subfolder: decisions, conventions, or ongoing work an agent can't infer. It never touches the root context files and refuses static reference folders.
howItWorks: Confirms the target is a subfolder and reads its key source, config, and Markdown.
Skips static reference folders and context that is easy to discover on demand.
Writes CLAUDE.md only from folder evidence or explicit user decisions; inherits root policy without repeating it.
Creates AGENTS.md as a symlink to CLAUDE.md, or a one-line pointer if symlinks fail.
Respects user edits; flags contradictions but never reverts them unless asked.
useWhen: A monorepo package has conventions or MUST NOTs that differ from root.
A folder has locked decisions or long-running work the next session must know.
You want local constraints followed without bloating the root CLAUDE.md.
avoidWhen: Editing the root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md: use /ak:docs agent-context.
The folder holds only static reference material or easily discovered context.
Recording session history: use ak-journal.

params.name: <target-folder>
params.desc: Required: subfolder to document; must not be the project root. Writes only inside it.

examples.note: Billing package with its own currency-handling constraints.
Record the MUST NOT refactor rule and why.

tips: Useful content: purpose, key files, MUST NOTs, naming, dated decisions, cross-session context.
Use bullets; no directory trees, repeated root rules, or credentials.

ak-interview-docs.tagline: Interview the user and turn their vision and decisions into docs.
ak-interview-docs.summary: ak:interview-docs turns your knowledge and decisions into a README, ADR, strategy, principles, or other structured doc, patching it after every answer. It never invents content or derives docs from code.
howItWorks: Picks vision mode (README, decisions) or structured-doc mode (principles, strategy); asks once if both fit.
Finds the existing owner doc via README and docs navigation; doesn't assume docs/adr exists.
Asks one focused question per turn on open decisions and patches the doc after each answer.
Keeps your wording; treats your lists as unordered until you set priority.
useWhen: Write a README that states the project vision in the founder's words.
Record decisions you already made, as ADRs if the repo uses them.
Draft principles or strategy when ideas exist but lack structure.
avoidWhen: You want AI to propose and compare options: use ak-brainstorm.
The doc should be derived from code: use ak-docs.
You need a research brief for someone else: use ak-research-prompt.

params.name: <vision | document-path | topic>
params.desc: Required: a vision statement, a doc path to build or finish, or a structured-doc topic.

examples.note: Vision mode: interview to write a direction-setting README.
Structured-doc mode, one question at a time.

tips: Tentative opinions never become decisions; ADRs hold only settled choices.
The doc is patched after each answer, so you can stop midway.

ak-llms.tagline: Generate llms.txt and llms-full.txt per llmstxt.org from docs or a URL.
ak-llms.summary: ak:llms builds an LLM-friendly Markdown index of your docs per the llmstxt.org spec, optionally with an inline llms-full.txt. It doesn't handle hosting, SEO, robots.txt, or sitemaps.
howItWorks: Builds an allowlist of public sources from README and site navigation, or the structure of a URL.
Takes titles from navigation or H1, summarizes real content, and groups pages as core or optional.
Generates with scripts/generate-llms-txt.py or by hand: H1, summary blockquote, H2 link sections, ## Optional last.
Validates structure, links, and short jargon-free descriptions.
useWhen: You publish a docs site and want AI tools to find it.
You need a compact context file, or llms-full.txt for one-shot loading.
avoidWhen: Updating llms.txt within the general docs workflow: use /ak:docs llms.
Looking up external library docs: use ak-docs-seeker.
Mintlify sites needing AI features configured: use ak-mintlify.

params.name: [path|url]
params.desc: Folder, file, or docs URL to scan. Omitted: discovered from README, site config, and navigation.

params.name: --full
params.desc: Also generate llms-full.txt with inline content.

params.name: --output path
params.desc: Output location; default project root.

params.name: --url base
params.desc: Base URL prefix for links (https://example.com/docs); maps to the script's --base-url.

examples.note: Discover docs and write llms.txt at root.
Write to the public folder with absolute links.

tips: Put changelogs and legacy under ## Optional; agents may skip it on short context.
Summarize real page content; first paragraphs are often boilerplate.

ak-markdown-novel-viewer.tagline: Read markdown in a calm, book-like viewer over local HTTP.
ak-markdown-novel-viewer.summary: ak:markdown-novel-viewer serves a Markdown file or folder from a local Node server as a book-style reader with themes, progress bar, and plan navigation. It returns a localhost URL; HTML generation belongs to ak:preview --html.
howItWorks: Reuses a known server for the project; checks processes and ports before starting one.
Runs scripts/server.cjs with --file or --dir, binds to localhost, and returns the printed URL.
Records PID and port; stops only its own server when done.
useWhen: Read a long RFC, design doc, or report without distractions.
Browse a multi-phase plan with status sidebar and Previous/Next navigation.
avoidWhen: Generating HTML explainers or slides: use ak-preview.
A kanban plan dashboard: use ak-plans-kanban.
Reading a few lines; the terminal is enough.

params.name: [file-or-directory]
params.desc: Markdown file (maps to --file) or folder (maps to --dir).

params.name: --file <path>
params.desc: Markdown file to view.

params.name: --dir <path>
params.desc: Folder to browse.

params.name: --port <number>
params.desc: Server port, default 3456.

params.name: --host <addr>
params.desc: Bind host, default localhost; 0.0.0.0 only when remote access is asked.

params.name: --open
params.desc: Open the browser automatically; default off.

params.name: --background
params.desc: Run in the background; default off.

params.name: --stop
params.desc: Stops ALL viewer servers; use only if all are yours, else stop your PID.

examples.note: Read a long RFC in the browser.
Browse a multi-phase plan.

tips: Shortcuts: ? cheatsheet, T theme, S sidebar, ←/→ switch phase, Esc close.
Always use the URL the server prints; it may not be port 3456.
artifacts: No files; a local Node server process (track PID and port)

ak-mintlify.tagline: Build and maintain Mintlify docs: docs.json, MDX, navigation, OpenAPI.
ak-mintlify.summary: ak:mintlify edits Mintlify sites (docs.json, MDX pages, navigation, theme, OpenAPI, AI assets) and runs validation. It uses the project's CLI and version-matched docs, never a global install.
howItWorks: Inspects docs root, manifest, lockfile, config, and installed CLI version before choosing commands.
Routes by change (config, content, navigation, OpenAPI, deploy, AI) to one reference file.
Runs installed validators (mint validate, mint broken-links, mint a11y, mint openapi-check).
Reuses a running preview, stops processes it started, and deploys only to a requested target.
useWhen: Add MDX pages with Mintlify components or reorganize docs.json navigation.
Generate API reference pages from OpenAPI/AsyncAPI.
Configure llms.txt, skill.md, or MCP, or add link and a11y CI checks.
avoidWhen: The project doesn't use Mintlify: use ak-docs.
A standalone llms.txt: use ak-llms.
Deploying an app to general hosting: use ak-deploy.

params.name: [task]
params.desc: Work to do (config, content, navigation, OpenAPI, deploy, AI); decides which reference loads.

params.name: [path]
params.desc: Docs root or file to edit.

examples.note: New MDX page added to navigation.
Generate API reference from OpenAPI.

tips: Don't install a global CLI or run init just to edit one MDX file.
Mintlify auto-deploys from Git; other targets need a static build and proof.
Stop any mint dev process you started so it frees the port.

ak-diagram.tagline: Compile typed JSON IR into SVG, fragments, or interactive HTML readers.
ak-diagram.summary: ak:diagram compiles a typed JSON IR offline into deterministic SVG, an HTML fragment, or a self-contained interactive reader. You describe topology; the compiler handles layout, routing, and role-based styling.
howItWorks: Pick an archetype: architecture, workflow, sequence, dataflow, or lifecycle, then write the IR envelope.
Placement comes from IR fields (layer, lane, stage.order, initial state), never coordinates.
Compiles with scripts/compiler/compile.mjs; render.py also accepts Mermaid or legacy templates.
Same IR gives byte-identical output with no overlaps; animation is CSS-only, under 8 s.
The HTML reader adds search, focus, shortest path, role filter, chapters, and theme toggle.
useWhen: Architecture or multi-lane workflows as an interactive, searchable reader.
API sequences, data pipelines, or state machines without hand-placing coordinates.
Deterministic output to commit and diff in review.
avoidWhen: Editable whiteboard sketches: use ak-excalidraw.
Static publication-grade diagrams: use ak-tech-graph.
Inline markdown diagrams: use ak-mermaidjs-v11.

params.name: [input-file]
params.desc: Typed JSON IR file; render.py also takes Mermaid .mmd (vendored v11.4.1) or legacy templates.

params.name: --format <svg|fragment|html>
params.desc: svg: clean vector. fragment: scoped HTML for an existing page. html: self-contained interactive reader.

params.name: --preset <classic|signal-flow|blueprint|editorial>
params.desc: Visual preset, not meaning: classic (default), signal-flow (glow), blueprint (technical grid), editorial (warm serif).

params.name: --theme <light|dark>
params.desc: Light or dark; the reader has a toggle.

params.name: --out <path>
params.desc: Output file path; for render.py, an output folder.

examples.note: Dark interactive reader for an architecture.
Vector SVG for docs.
The skill picks the archetype and writes the IR.

tips: Steer placement with layer, lane, stage.order, or initial state; never declare coordinates.
Reader keys: / search, R shortest path, L role filter, F present, [ ] chapters.
Compile errors usually mean a wrong role enum or invalid ID characters.

ak-excalidraw.tagline: Draw editable Excalidraw diagrams via live MCP canvas or rendered files.
ak-excalidraw.summary: ak:excalidraw makes editable diagrams for architecture, data flow, and system design, using a live MCP canvas when available or a .excalidraw file rendered to PNG with Playwright. It can auto-diagram a repo.
howItWorks: Uses the MCP canvas (Mode A) if it works, else file mode (Mode B); guides setup if neither works.
Maps concepts to visual patterns (fan-out, tree, timeline, cycle) and plans layout direction.
Repo auto-diagram: discovers components and connections, capped at 12 components and 20 arrows.
Renders, self-critiques overlap, clipped text, and wrong arrows, then fixes over 2-4 rounds.
useWhen: The user says 'diagram this repo' or 'visualize the architecture'.
The diagram must stay editable in Excalidraw.
Draw a concept or system design live with the user.
avoidWhen: Validated system maps with an interactive reader: use ak-diagram.
Static publication-grade diagrams: use ak-tech-graph.
Inline markdown diagrams: use ak-mermaidjs-v11.

params.name: [diagram description|path]
params.desc: Diagram description, a .excalidraw file to edit or render, or a folder/repo to auto-diagram.

params.name: --export <png|svg>
params.desc: Export PNG or SVG; file mode renders PNG (--scale 2, --width 1920). Per-mode mapping is undocumented.

params.name: --live
params.desc: Use the live MCP canvas (Mode A); undocumented, since the skill auto-detects mode.

examples.note: Auto-diagram the current codebase.

examples.cmd: /ak:excalidraw OAuth flow between client, API, and IdP --export png
examples.note: Data-flow diagram as PNG.
Draw on the MCP canvas.

tips: File mode needs uv and Playwright Chromium; MCP mode needs a running canvas and mcp-excalidraw-server.
Avoid cramped spacing: boxes 200-240px, labeled arrow gaps 150-200px, rows 280-350px.
Use 3-4 fill colors; same role, same color. Keep IDs and palette when editing.
artifacts: SVG/PNG exported from the MCP canvas

ak-mermaidjs-v11.tagline: Write Mermaid.js v11 diagrams: flowchart, sequence, ER, Gantt, state, and more.
ak-mermaidjs-v11.summary: ak:mermaidjs-v11 writes Mermaid v11 text diagrams (24+ types) as inline code blocks, exporting SVG/PNG/PDF with mermaid-cli only when needed. It's the lightest diagram option for docs, READMEs, and PRs.
howItWorks: Picks a diagram type and writes it, with optional frontmatter config (theme, look).
For Markdown hosts outputs a mermaid code block; checks host support for newer v11 features.
Exports only on request with mmdc (-i/-o, -t theme, -b background) and checks the result.
useWhen: Inline diagrams in a README, docs, or PR description.
ER diagrams for a schema or sequence diagrams for an API flow.
avoidWhen: Validated interactive system maps: use ak-diagram.
Publication-grade styled diagrams: use ak-tech-graph.
Complex data charts: use the dataviz skill.

params.name: [diagram-type or description]
params.desc: Mermaid diagram type (flowchart, erDiagram) or a description of what to illustrate.

examples.cmd: /ak:mermaidjs-v11 sequence of the OAuth login flow
examples.note: Sequence diagram for a README.

examples.cmd: /ak:mermaidjs-v11 flowchart for order processing, export SVG
examples.note: Export with mmdc.

tips: Inline use needs no CLI; install @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli only to export images.
Common errors: -> instead of -->, or a mistyped diagram type; test on mermaid.live.

ak-tech-graph.tagline: Generate publication-grade SVG+PNG technical diagrams in 7 visual styles.
ak-tech-graph.summary: ak:tech-graph creates technical diagrams (architecture, data flow, sequence, agent/memory, UML, ER, network, and more) as SVG plus 1920px PNG. Styles include Flat Icon (default), Dark Terminal, Blueprint, Notion Clean, Glassmorphism, Claude Official, and OpenAI Official.
howItWorks: Recovers entities and relations from source or your description; flags uncertain ones.
Keeps any supplied style, else Flat Icon; loads style and layout-rule references.
Builds SVG from a template helper or by hand, then exports PNG via rsvg-convert.
Inspects the export for collisions and clipped text, fixes, and reports real validation status.
useWhen: Polished diagrams for blogs, articles, or slides.
Illustrate RAG pipelines, multi-agent systems, or memory layers, including Anthropic/OpenAI house style.
avoidWhen: Inline markdown diagrams: use ak-mermaidjs-v11.
Interactive HTML readers: use ak-diagram.
Editable canvas: use ak-excalidraw.

params.name: [diagram-type or system description]
params.desc: Diagram type (architecture, flowchart, sequence, agent, UML, ER, network, and more) or a system description.

params.name: --output /path/
params.desc: Custom output folder; default ./[derived-name].svg and .png in the current folder.

examples.cmd: /ak:tech-graph architecture of a RAG system with a vector DB
examples.note: Default Flat Icon style.
Anthropic house style.

tips: Requires rsvg-convert (librsvg); verify it before promising PNG.
Use helper scripts for complex SVG to avoid syntax errors.

ak-show-off.tagline: Build self-contained HTML showcase pages with section screenshots and publishing.
ak-show-off.summary: ak:show-off builds a responsive HTML showcase from markdown or a prompt, with fact-checked content, section screenshots in three aspect ratios, and optional agentwiki publishing. It remembers your screenshot, publishing, and language preferences.
howItWorks: Loads saved preferences (default: screenshots on, publishing on, vi+en) and saves changes unless 'just this once'.
Splits the request into 2-6 sections, fact-checks online, and writes content.md with citations.
Builds HTML with ak:frontend-design and ak:diagram, plus AntV and diagram-design visuals unless disabled.
Captures per-section screenshots, runs a 5-point quality gate, publishes if enabled, and opens the page.
useWhen: Show off a finished feature with a polished page.
You need section images at 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 for social media.
Build a bilingual Vietnamese-English showcase with cited sources.
avoidWhen: Explaining code or internal slides: use ak-preview.
Real product UI: use ak-frontend-design.
Reading long markdown: use ak-markdown-novel-viewer.

params.name: [markdown-or-prompt]
params.desc: Markdown content or a prompt describing the showcase.

params.name: --no-antv

params.name: --no-diagram-design
params.desc: Disable diagram-design section diagrams.

params.name: --no-editorial-visuals
params.desc: Disable all editorial visuals (AntV and diagram-design); the hero still uses ak:frontend-design.

params.name: --no-screenshots
params.desc: Skip section screenshots; saved as a preference unless just this run.

params.name: --no-publish
params.desc: Keep local: no agentwiki publish or rws fallback; saved unless just this run.

params.name: --languages en|vi|en,vi
params.desc: Content language: vi,en bilingual with toggle, or en/vi single-language.

params.name: preferences.js set|get|reset
params.desc: Preference helper at $AGENTKIT_HOME/show-off/preferences.json (override SHOW_OFF_PREFS_PATH); set toggles screenshots, publishing, and languages.

examples.cmd: /ak:show-off introduce the realtime sync feature we just shipped
examples.note: Full showcase per saved preferences.

examples.cmd: /ak:show-off demo dashboard, English only, local only
examples.note: English, no publishing; saved as preference.

examples.cmd: /ak:show-off new system architecture, no screenshots this time
examples.note: Skip screenshots once.

tips: Local capture needs Node and headless Chrome; rws fallback needs RWEB_API_KEY, never on the command line.
Publishing needs the agentwiki CLI; say 'local only' once and it's remembered.

ak-copywriting.tagline: Conversion copy: headlines, emails, landing pages, CTAs, style extraction.
ak-copywriting.summary: Writes high-converting copy for an agreed deliverable, audience, goal, and brand voice. Ships formulas (AIDA, PAS, BAB), templates, 30 writing styles, and a style-extraction script.
howItWorks: Reads deliverable, audience, goal, and voice from the brief; asks only when it changes the copy.
Uses formulas as optional structure; brand voice wins.
Ties every claim, number, or testimonial to evidence; never invents social proof.
useWhen: Headlines, landing pages, CTAs, or emails that must convert.
Applying a custom writing style from assets/writing-styles/.
avoidWhen: Developer docs or CLAUDE.md: use ak-docs.
An HTML product showcase page: use ak-show-off.

params.name: [copy-type]
params.desc: Copy type: headline, landing page, email, CTA, social, product description.

params.name: [context]
params.desc: Product, audience, offer, brand voice, constraints.

examples.note: A batch of headlines.

examples.cmd: /ak:copywriting landing-page "CRM for agencies, audience: owners of 5–20 person agencies"
examples.note: Landing page structure and copy.

tips: scripts/extract-writing-styles.py saves a style from sample files into assets/writing-styles/.
Unsupported claims are flagged as suggestions, not stated as fact.
artifacts: Copy at the requested path (fallback assets/copy/{type}/)
